payload.title: Isekai: Harem System
payload.blurb: Valdris is a trade city at the foot of the Crimson Range, where caravans bring ore and spirit beast heartstones down from the high passes. Yesterday you woke there as the youngest of House Ashworth, a noble house with more debts than servants, remembering a whole life on Earth and seeing a window…
payload.overview: Valdris sits on a bend of the Ostrel river where the caravan road from the Crimson Range meets the salt road south. The city is built in two tiers. The Terrace holds the old noble houses behind pale walls, and Saltgate runs along the river below, a market of warehouses, iron yards and drying racks that opens before dawn. Everyone in Valdris is human. Power here is qi, the breath people draw from the world into a core in the body, and the trade that moves it. People cultivate in five stages: Stirring, Channel, Hearth, Tempered and Ascendant, which few reach in a lifetime. Sects teach cultivation and houses pay for it, and the Crimson Sect is the strongest of them. Spirit beasts from the Range supply the heartstones that alchemists grind into tonics. The city's gods are Aldun, who keeps roads, oaths and trade, and Immera, who keeps hearths and the dead. The System belongs to you alone. Nobody in Valdris has heard of it, and nobody else can see its windows. It shows you each person's attraction and the depth of your bond as numbers. It cannot make anyone feel anything, and it counts a bond only when both people have chosen it.
payload.intro:
The house of Ashworth is cold at the fourth bell, when the furnaces of Saltgate start up below the Terrace and the rest of the hill is still asleep. In the east hall a tray waits on the sideboard with a bill on it, the paper creased from being folded and unfolded. Ebbe Tollan, the steward, stands at the foot of the stairs with his hands folded behind him, which he does when the news is bad. When you look at him, a thin line of light hangs at the edge of your sight. He cannot see it.

The bill is from the Saltgate Caravan Guild, and it falls due at the end of the month. Folded inside it is a second letter, sealed in the Crimson Sect's black wax, with a date two weeks off and your name in a clerk's neat hand.

"The Guild's man will call at noon," Ebbe says. "As the house wishes, I will tell him whatever you tell me." He holds out the tray.
starters:
The Blue Kettle is empty at the fifth bell, its chairs stacked on the tables and the floor still wet from the night's mopping. Jory Pell sits on the end of the bar with his boots on a stool, sharpening a short knife he has no use for. In the kitchen his aunt is arguing with the cook about the price of salt. Last night you bet Jory a silver crown that you could lift the tavern's iron-bound barrel alone, and you did, with a breath he had never seen anyone draw. His aunt wants the crown kept in the till.

Jory sees you in the doorway, puts the knife down, and sends the crown spinning along the bar until it stops against your hand.

"Yours," he says. "Or double it. A copper says you can't tell me how you did that, and another says you won't."

The east gate of Valdris opens onto the Crimson road at the sixth bell, and the carts coming down from the Range are already queued three deep. Hanne Valk waits beside the gatehouse in the black-and-red coat of a Crimson Sect disciple, a spear upright at her shoulder and two days' dust on her boots. She came down alone, which the sect does not allow. Behind her a line of carts creaks toward the tanners, ashwing heartstones already cut out and bagged.

She has been watching faces. When she sees yours she steps into your way with the spear held crosswise.

"Ashworth," she says. "Yesterday you came through this gate breathing qi like nobody I have met in two years on the mountain. Who taught you?"

The Marrec counting house fills the ground floor of a narrow house on the Terrace: six clerks at six desks, a clock loud enough to keep time by, and at the back, under the one good window, Sidonie Marrec at a table with a contract open in front of her. She wears grey gloves and a pen behind one ear, and she does not look up when the clerk shows you in.

"Sit," she says, and turns the contract round so you can read it. It is a betrothal between House Marrec and House Varenne, signed by both fathers and by Tibor Varenne. One line is blank: the witness, who by the Terrace's custom must come from a third house that owes neither.

She takes off her right glove. "Every house on this hill owes Varenne money but yours. Will you sign?"

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 21, the youngest of House Ashworth, a declining house on the Terrace with more debts than servants. Until yesterday you were someone else, with another name and a whole life on Earth, and the household has begun to notice the change. Ebbe Tollan the steward keeps the ledgers, the Saltgate Guild holds the house's notes, and the Crimson Sect's summons to its trial is due in two weeks.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
House Varenne - a rising house with a seat on the Trade Board, which wants the Ashworth name off the Terrace.
The Crimson Sect - the strongest cultivation school in the Range, which wants disciples who can survive the vents.
The Saltgate Caravan Guild - the lenders of the river market, which want their notes paid in coin or in land.
House Marrec - an old counting house on the Terrace, which wants a seat on the Trade Board through the Varenne match.

entries.title: Valdris in one breath
entries.content: Valdris is a trade city at the foot of the Crimson Range, on the Ostrel river. Caravans bring ore and spirit beast heartstones down from the passes to sell to lowland buyers. Everyone there is human. The city has two tiers: the Terrace of noble houses above, and Saltgate, the warehouse market by the river below. Its power is qi, and the money that buys it.

entries.title: The System
entries.content: A System came with you from Earth: a window at the edge of your sight that nobody else can see or has heard of. It shows each person's attraction to you and the depth of your bond, and it lends you strength, Bond Power, from the bonds you earn. It cannot touch anyone but you. It never makes a person feel anything, and it counts a bond only when both people chose it.

entries.title: The Terrace and Saltgate
entries.content: The Terrace crowns the hill: old houses behind pale walls, their gardens facing the mountains, House Ashworth among them. Saltgate runs along the river below: warehouses, iron yards, drying racks and the Blue Kettle by the river stairs. Pestle Row climbs between them, a street of alchemists and glass lamps. The east gate opens on the Crimson road, and the salt road runs south.

entries.title: House Ashworth
entries.content: House Ashworth is a minor house on the Terrace: four floors of grey stone, a small vineyard of sour wine, and a Trade Board seat empty for ten years. It runs on Guild credit. Lady Gisela Ashworth, 56, a widow, keeps to her rooms. The elder two, Mattis, 29, and Gerda, 26, left Valdris years ago. You, at 21, are the youngest, and the one the sect has written to.

entries.title: The east hall
entries.content: The east hall of House Ashworth has a cold hearth, a sideboard where the day's letters wait on a tray, and the main stair down to the drive. At the fourth bell the furnaces of Saltgate start up and their glow comes through the east windows. Ebbe Tollan, 52, steward for thirty years, waits there each morning with the bills.

entries.title: People of the first days
entries.content: Jory Pell, 20, tends bar at the Blue Kettle for his aunt, Agna Pell, 46. Hanne Valk, 25, is a Crimson Sect disciple. On Pestle Row, Wolter Kroll, 27, grinds heartstones, and Eskil Lunde, 63, once a sect instructor, lodges above the dye shop. Sidonie Marrec, 24, runs her family's counting house; Iva Dahlke, 22, keeps her father's caravan books.

entries.title: Bonds and Harem Rank
entries.content: Every bond the System sees has a tier: Stranger, Known, Close, Devoted, Bonded. It deepens only when both people choose it, through time, kept promises and danger shared, and it may be a friend's, an ally's or a lover's. Harem Rank is one, plus one for each bond at Close or deeper; it rises when a bond first reaches Close and falls when a bond at Close or deeper breaks. The System takes no candidate under twenty.

entries.title: The first quest
entries.content: The System's first quest appeared the first time you looked into its window: earn one person's trust to Close within seven days. If no bond has reached Close by the seventh dawn, the System goes dark and does not come back. Later quests are plain and small: keep a promise, share a danger, tell one true thing. A finished quest raises Bond Power, never Harem Rank.

entries.title: Qi and the five stages
entries.content: Qi is the breath of the world, drawn in through the meridians and stored in a core. People advance in five stages: Stirring, when qi first moves under the skin; Channel, when it runs the meridians; Hearth, when a core forms; Tempered, when it hardens; Ascendant, which few ever reach. Each stage costs years of teaching and a fortune in heartstones.

entries.title: The Quenching
entries.content: The Quenching is the Crimson Sect's yearly trial at the cinder vents high in the Range: candidates pass it to enter, and disciples pass it again to rise. The sect takes no candidate under twenty. Candidates draw qi from the vents while ashwings, cart-sized beasts that shed ash, circle the cave, and one who breaks their stance is carried down the mountain. A pass lifts a family's standing for a generation. This year's falls in two weeks.

entries.title: The Crimson Sect
entries.content: The Crimson Sect teaches cultivation from a hall cut into the highest shelf of the Crimson Range, and its disciples wear black and red. It sells heartstones to lowland houses and lends them its name. It wants disciples who can survive the vents and cares little for the families that send them. Its rules bar disciples from forming bonds before their trials.

entries.title: House Varenne
entries.content: House Varenne is a rising house with a Trade Board seat and wagons on the salt road. Its heir, Tibor Varenne, 24, is betrothed to Sidonie Marrec. It wants the Ashworth name off the Terrace and the Ashworth lands on its books. Its friends say it pays its debts early. Its enemies say it buys them first.

entries.title: The Saltgate Caravan Guild
entries.content: The Saltgate Caravan Guild moves most of the goods that enter and leave Valdris. It lends to houses that cannot pay the sect and sells their notes when they fail. Its masters keep a fair ledger, remember every debt and tell nobody who bought what. It wants its notes paid in coin, and it takes land when it must.

entries.title: Names in Valdris
entries.content: Valdris writes a given name first, then the house: Sidonie Marrec is Sidonie of House Marrec. Given names are short and old: Hanne, Iva, Wolter, Jory, Ebbe, Gisela, Corran, Mirela, Pieter, Oda. Streets take the name of the trade that works them, and houses the names of their founders.

entries.title: The gods of Valdris
entries.content: Aldun the Gatekeeper is god of roads, oaths and trade, and every caravan pays a coin at his shrine by the gate. Immera the Quiet Hearth keeps homes, harvests and the dead, and Saltgate lights her lamps at dusk. The Red Mother, the old spirit of the Range, is said to sleep under the peaks, and the sect does not speak her name aloud.

entries.title: The Ashfall Year
entries.content: Valdris counts its years from its founding, and this is the year 472. In 412 a ridge fell in the Crimson Range and opened three new cinder vents, and ash lay on the Terrace for a season. The Ashfall Year cut the caravans off for a winter and made Valdris rich in heartstones. People still argue whether the sect caused the fall or only profited from it.

entries.title: Ashwings
entries.content: Ashwings are spirit beasts the size of a cart, with grey wings that shed ash and a heartstone in the chest. They nest near the cinder vents and hunt in pairs. Their hearts are the most valued heartstones in Valdris, and a wounded ashwing will circle a camp for days. Caravan guards carry torches burning with qi to keep them off the road.

entries.title: Shared breath
entries.content: Two people who trust each other can breathe qi together, sitting palm to palm, and both grow stronger; the weaker gains more. It works only as far as the trust goes, so strangers who try it feel nothing. The sects teach it cautiously and forbid it to disciples before their trials. The System rewards it, and nobody in Valdris knows a faster road to Bond Power.

entries.title: Heartstones and alchemy
entries.content: A heartstone is the core a spirit beast leaves behind when it dies. It holds qi that alchemists grind into tonics, pills and salves. Pestle Row sells them by weight, and the purest come with a receipt from the sect. Counterfeit heartstones of glass and dye are a crime the Watch punishes hard, and every alchemist on the Row claims never to have seen one.

entries.title: The Crimson Range
entries.content: The Crimson Range rises behind Valdris, its rock red with iron, and its high passes stay open only in summer. Cinder vents steam along the ridges, and spirit beasts hunt the slopes below them. Miners cut heartstones from the beasts they kill. The sect's hall sits on the highest shelf of the Range, reached by a road of seventeen switchbacks.

entries.title: The Blue Kettle
entries.content: The Blue Kettle is a Saltgate tavern by the river stairs: low beams, a long bar, and a back room where porters wrestle for coppers on rest-day nights. Its keeper, Agna Pell, 46, hears every rumor on the river. A letter left at the bar reaches half the warehouses by noon, and Agna decides which half.

entries.title: The Marrec counting house
entries.content: House Marrec is old money with no Board seat: its counting house on the Terrace keeps the books of half the hill and lends quietly to the rest. Sidonie Marrec, 24, runs it for her father. Her betrothal to Tibor Varenne would give the Marrecs a seat on the Trade Board. By the Terrace's custom, a betrothal needs a witness from a third house that owes neither.

entries.title: The Trade Board
entries.content: The Trade Board sets the tolls, the weights and the market days of Valdris. It has seven seats, held by Terrace houses and Guild masters, and it sits in the Hall of Scales by the east gate at each new moon. House Ashworth's seat has stood empty for ten years. A seat left empty for twelve is given to another house.

world.vibe: Crisp and mercantile, smoke and ledgers under every courtesy. People talk about debts when they mean fear, about qi when they mean envy, and about the view when they mean they like you.

opening.note: Staged, over the first three turns. Beat one: the east hall of House Ashworth at the fourth bell, before dawn, the furnaces of Saltgate starting below. Ebbe Tollan speaks first. He wants the player to take the Guild bill and say what the house will tell the Guild's man at noon, and he has noticed the change in the player overnight without saying so. The Crimson Sect letter inside the bill is not discussed until the player opens it. The System never speaks aloud. Its window shows as a thin line of light at the edge of the player's sight when they look at a person or a letter, and nobody else reacts to it. The first time the player looks into it, it sets its first quest: earn one person's trust to Close within seven days. Say that once, plainly, and do not count the days aloud. Beat two: before the player can answer, Tibor Varenne's carriage stops in the drive below, and Tibor comes up the steps uninvited with a bottle of good wine, offering to help the family with its arithmetic. He is charming, and he means harm. Beat three: by the third turn the player has three people to go to and a reason for each: Jory Pell at the Blue Kettle in Saltgate, who owes a silver crown; Hanne Valk at the Crimson road gate, who wants to know who taught the player to breathe; and Wolter Kroll on Pestle Row, who will sell a reagent for a price. Name the three places plainly. Nobody warms to the player because of the System, and nobody is ever made to: every bit of warmth is earned in the scene.

cast.name: Ebbe Tollan
cast.role: Steward of House Ashworth for thirty years, who knows exactly how much the house owes and to whom; this week he wants the Guild bill answered before the month is out.
cast.look: stout and grey at the temples, side-whiskers trimmed square, a black coat rubbed shiny at the cuffs, a brass key ring at his hip
cast.manner: Speaks in the old formal court style the house can no longer afford, finishing every sentence however long it takes. Says 'as the house wishes' when he disagrees. Folds his hands behind his back when he is worried.
cast.secret: He has been selling the house's old sect seal, a black token from your grandfather's time, to a Varenne agent to pay the grain bills, and he keeps the money in a tin under the cellar stairs.

cast.name: Eskil Lunde
cast.role: Retired instructor of the Crimson Sect, living in two rooms above a dye shop on Pestle Row; he teaches anyone who climbs his stairs and pays in bread.
cast.look: long-boned and bald under a felt cap, a burn-scarred left hand he flexes while he thinks, grey eyes that seem never to blink
cast.manner: Asks about your breathing before he asks your name. Speaks in short sayings he makes up on the spot and then explains at length. Peels a boiled egg with great care while he listens.
cast.secret: The sect dismissed him for teaching shared breath to outsiders. He knows what a System window is because forty years ago he saw one in a disciple of twenty-two whom the sect's records no longer mention.

cast.name: Hanne Valk
cast.role: Second-year disciple of the Crimson Sect, down from the Range ahead of the Quenching; drawn to you because you moved qi in a way she cannot name, she holds back because sect rules bar disciples from bonds before their trials.
cast.look: tall and sun-hard, white-blonde hair cropped at the jaw, a red scar through one brow, the sect's black-and-red coat buttoned to the neck
cast.manner: Clipped and dry, in a soldier's short sentences. Keeps her spear in hand indoors and answers anything about the sect in the sect's own words, word for word. Never accepts the first offer of anything, food included.
cast.secret: She failed the Quenching last year and was told to keep silent. Her brother Joren, twenty-three, took the place she lost and died on the ridge in his first month, and the sect wrote it up as a fall.

cast.name: Sidonie Marrec
cast.role: Lady of House Marrec, who runs the family counting house on the Terrace and reads every contract it signs; drawn to you because you do not flatter her, she holds back because she is promised to Tibor Varenne.
cast.look: pale and straight-backed, black hair dressed high under silver pins, long gloves of grey leather, a ledger pen tucked behind one ear
cast.manner: Precise and unhurried, in short questions and long pauses. Quotes clauses of contracts word for word. Takes off one glove, never both, when she means to deal seriously.
cast.secret: Her father did not promise her to Varenne to settle a debt, as the Terrace says. She proposed the match herself, to win her house a seat on the Trade Board, and she has begun to wish she had not.

cast.name: Iva Dahlke
cast.role: A merchant's daughter who keeps the books for her father's caravans in Saltgate; drawn to you because you never cheated her at the scales, she holds back because she is sure every noble wants her money.
cast.look: freckled and quick, brown curls tied up in a red kerchief, ink on two fingers, a canvas coat with a dozen pockets, each holding a different coin
cast.manner: Fast and funny, and answers before you finish asking, right about half the time. Knows every coin by the town that struck it and says so. Says no before she thinks, then yes a moment later, once she has.
cast.secret: Her father bought the Ashworth notes from the Guild last month and put them in her name. She can call in your house's debt any day she likes, and she is waiting to see whether you are worth the risk of not doing it.

cast.name: Wolter Kroll
cast.role: Alchemist on Pestle Row who grinds heartstones into tonics for the Terrace houses; drawn to you because you named a reagent he could not, he holds back because a Varenne man pays him to keep certain tonics weak.
cast.look: narrow and tall with a stoop, a pale face flecked green from his work, hair cut short with a kitchen knife, stained hands kept in his apron pockets
cast.manner: Softly spoken. Trails off mid-sentence when a problem catches him and picks it up minutes later exactly where he stopped. Sniffs everything before he touches it, letters included.
cast.secret: Not every heartstone he sells the Terrace was cut from a beast killed in the Range. Some he grew in his cellar from shards a Varenne courier brings him, and he has never told a buyer which.

cast.name: Jory Pell
cast.role: Nephew of the Blue Kettle's keeper, who works the bar, runs the back-room wrestling and carries letters for half of Saltgate; drawn to you since you won his barrel bet, he holds back because his aunt will not let him leave the Kettle.
cast.look: broad-shouldered and easy, a crooked grin, sandy hair falling in his eyes, a split knuckle he never mentions, a leather apron over a red shirt
cast.manner: Loud until he is interested, then quiet. Turns any question into a wager, a copper on the answer. Sits on whatever is nearest that is not a chair.
cast.secret: For a month he has carried sealed letters from Tibor Varenne to his own aunt, Agna. He has opened and resealed every one, and he is close to cracking the Varenne cipher on the back of a bar tab.

cast.name: Tibor Varenne
cast.role: Heir of House Varenne, the rising house with a seat on the Trade Board, and betrothed to Sidonie Marrec; your rival for the Ashworth notes, he would rather take the Ashworth lands than pay for them.
cast.look: tall and polished, a fitted coat of plum velvet, silver cufflinks shaped like scales, a close-trimmed beard, a smile that stays put when his eyes do not
cast.manner: Polite, quick and cutting, with a habit of asking after your health in front of other people. Lifts his glass to you before he drinks and never finishes a bottle.
cast.secret: He offered the Guild double for the Ashworth notes and was told they were already sold. He does not know to whom, he believes it was the Marrecs, and he means to own the debt before the Quenching, so the Ashworth name comes off the Terrace without a fight.

systems.label: Bond Power
systems.meaning: The strength the System lends you from your bonds: qi drawn from the trust between you and the people bonded to you. It takes nothing from them.
systems.change: Rises each time a bond reaches a new tier and when a System quest is finished. Falls when a bond breaks or a quest is failed.

systems.label: Harem Rank
systems.meaning: Your rank under the System: one, plus one for each bond at Close or deeper. It counts only bonds both people chose.
systems.change: Rises by one when a bond first reaches Close. Falls by one when a bond at Close or deeper breaks. Nothing else moves it, quests included.

systems.label: Days on the First Quest
systems.meaning: The days left on the System's first quest: earn one person's trust to Close, or the System goes dark for good.
systems.change: Falls by one at each dawn. Stops for good the moment any bond reaches Close.

systems.label: Standing on the Terrace
systems.meaning: How the Terrace and Saltgate speak of House Ashworth and of you, from scandal to standing.
systems.change: Rises after a debt paid in public or a promise kept before witnesses. Falls after a broken promise, an unpaid bill or a rumor carried to the Trade Board.

npcSystems.label: Attraction
npcSystems.meaning: How drawn this person is to you, from indifference to wanting your company for its own sake. It is theirs alone: the System can read it and cannot move it.
npcSystems.change: Rises with honest time together and with attention to what they care about. Falls when you are careless with their trust or press where you were not wanted.

npcSystems.label: Bond Level
npcSystems.meaning: The depth of the bond between you: 0 Stranger, 25 Known, 50 Close, 75 Devoted, 100 Bonded. A bond can be a friend's, an ally's or a lover's, and the System counts each the same.
npcSystems.change: Rises when both of you choose to trust each other further, through time together, a promise kept or a danger shared. Falls when the bond is broken.

style.art: Ink and gouache in rust red and cold blue, with a river at dusk and furnace glow in the windows. A typical picture shows one figure on a stone terrace above a city of lamps.

heroes.name: Aurel Ashworth
heroes.description: The youngest Ashworth, who was a hospice nurse on Earth and knows how to sit with someone through a hard hour without saying anything untrue.
heroes.look: Lean and dark-haired, a crooked nose from a fall off the Terrace wall, a coat cut for a better year.
heroes.background: The youngest of House Ashworth woke yesterday remembering a whole life on Earth. There Aurel worked night shifts as a hospice nurse, sitting with frightened people, listening, and telling them the truth gently. He does not yet know how far the house's debts go, or what happened to the Ashworth who was here before him.
heroes.carries: A signet ring with the house crest worn smooth and a sprig of dried feverfew in a coat pocket.

heroes.name: Wenna Ashworth
heroes.description: The youngest Ashworth, who worked six harvests in a vineyard on Earth and two years buying wine, and has tasted the house's sour vintage.
heroes.look: Small and quick, brown hair in a tight braid, sun-freckled hands, a riding coat with the house crest unpicked from the collar.
heroes.background: The youngest of House Ashworth woke yesterday remembering a whole life on Earth. There Wenna worked six harvests in a vineyard and then two years as a wine buyer, haggling with growers who lied about their soil. The Ashworth vines are small and the wine is sour, and she thinks she knows why.
heroes.carries: A signet ring with the house crest worn smooth and a silver tasting cup on a chain.

heroes.name: Lisle Ashworth
heroes.description: The youngest Ashworth, who ran the backstage of a touring theatre on Earth and can tell who is about to fall apart before they know it.
heroes.look: Tall and thin, black hair cropped close, dark watchful eyes, a plain grey coat kept buttoned, a habit of standing near the door of any room.
heroes.background: The youngest of House Ashworth woke yesterday remembering a whole life on Earth. There Lisle stage-managed a touring theatre for five years: calling cues, settling feuds between leads, and keeping a show running while it fell apart behind the curtain. A noble house in trouble feels familiar.
heroes.carries: A signet ring with the house crest worn smooth and a stub of pencil behind one ear.
